source: ACIAR AH/2005/086 'Smallholder Cattle Best Practice Manual' (Windsor, Bush & Young), Best Practice Health and Husbandry of Cattle, Cambodia -- hosted at mekonglivestock.wordpress.com (University of Sydney / GDAHP project site)
text: On vaccination specifically, the manual gives practical points often missed by smallholders: vaccines must be kept refrigerated (not frozen) right up until use, or they may become ineffective; most are given by injection under the skin; an initial dose plus a 'booster' 2-4 months later is typically needed, followed by annual revaccination for best protection; and every animal in a herd or village needs to be vaccinated for good herd-level protection, since partial coverage leaves gaps for disease to persist. Reasons a vaccinated animal can still get infected include: incorrect dosing or a missed booster, using expired vaccine, vaccine exposed to high temperatures in storage/transport, incomplete herd coverage, or a vaccine type that doesn't match the actual disease strain circulating.
